s1.title: About the service
s1.text: Tartib is a tracking and discipline tool for traders: a risk calculator, a trade journal, personal trading rules and statistics.

s2.title: Not advice
s2.text: Tartib does not provide investment advice, trading signals or profit guarantees. It is not a broker, a trading bot or an advisor. The trade score in the calculator only shows how well a trade fits your own rules and says nothing about where the market goes. You make your own trading decisions and are responsible for them. Trading on financial markets involves a risk of losing money.

s3.title: Account
s3.text: You are responsible for keeping your password safe and for the accuracy of the data you enter. One person, one account.

s4.title: Cost
s4.text: The service is free: there are no paid plans and no limits on the number of trades or rules. We will tell you in advance about any changes.

s5.title: Acceptable use
s5.text: You must not try to access other people's data, disrupt the service or use it for unlawful purposes.

s6.title: Limitation of liability
s6.text: The service is provided “as is”. Calculations are for reference: check them before you trade. We are not liable for losses related to trading or to using the service.

s7.title: Changes to the terms
s7.text: The terms may be updated. The current version is always available on this page.

s1.title: What data we store
s1.text: Email, name, settings (language, currency, time zone), trading accounts, rules, trades and your notes on them. We do not store your password: the Supabase authentication service handles it and keeps only a secure hash.

s2.title: Why we need it
s2.text: Only to make the calculator, the journal and the statistics work. We do not sell data or use it for advertising.

s3.title: Where data is stored
s3.text: In a Supabase database (PostgreSQL). Row-level security is on: each user can see and change only their own data.

s4.title: Who we share data with
s4.text: Only with services Tartib cannot work without: hosting and the database. If AI reports appear in the future, processing by an external AI provider will be switched on only with your consent, and we will tell you in advance.

s5.title: Cookies and browser storage
s5.text: We use cookies for signing in and your chosen language, and browser storage for your chosen theme. There are no advertising or third-party tracking cookies.

s6.title: Your rights
s6.text: You can change your name and settings in your profile. To delete your account with all data, contact us; the contact address will be published on the site before the public launch.

rr.title: Risk to reward calculator

streak.title: Losing streaks
streak.desc: How often long losing streaks happen even with a working strategy and what they do to your account.

o.single: Chance of such a streak at a given spot
o.atLeast: Chance of at least one such streak over these trades

streak.note: The calculation assumes independent trades with the same probability. In real life this is an approximation.

recovery.title: Drawdown recovery
recovery.desc: Why losing 50% is easy and getting it back is hard: how much growth you need after a drawdown.

compound.title: Compound growth
compound.desc: How an amount grows with a constant monthly return and deposits. A math illustration, not a forecast.
compound.note: Steady returns do not exist in trading. The result only shows the arithmetic of percentages.

sessions.title: Trading sessions and market hours
sessions.desc: Which market sessions are open right now in Sydney, Tokyo, London and New York, and how long until they open or close.
sessions.overlap: Two sessions are running at once: {names}.
sessions.note: Hours are typical for the Forex market and follow daylight saving time. A specific exchange may differ; weekends are Saturday and Sunday.

kelly.title: Kelly criterion
kelly.desc: What share of your account is mathematically worth risking per trade, given your win rate and reward-to-risk ratio.
kelly.note: Full Kelly means big drawdowns. Practitioners use half or a quarter. If expectancy is negative the result is 0%: there is nothing to bet.

ruin.title: Risk of ruin
ruin.desc: The probability that, at a given risk per trade, your account ever falls to the chosen drawdown. It shows why position risk matters more than entries.

o.cushion: Cushion, losing trades in a row

ruin.note: The model assumes independent trades with constant probability and risk. It is an approximation, not a forecast.

liq.title: Liquidation price
liq.desc: The approximate price at which an isolated leveraged position is force-closed by the exchange.
liq.note: Approximate: exchanges include fees and use their own formulas. Check the price on your exchange before trading.

fee.title: Break-even with fees
fee.desc: The price at which a trade with entry and exit fees ends at zero.
fee.note: Spread and slippage are not included.

profit.title: Trade result
profit.desc: Profit or loss of a trade including fees.

goal.title: Goal planner
goal.desc: How many months it takes to reach a target at a steady monthly return with deposits.
goal.note: Trading returns are never steady. This is percentage arithmetic, not a forecast or a promise.

margin.title: Margin and leverage
margin.desc: How much of your own money a leveraged position needs and what share of your account it takes.
margin.note: Higher leverage puts liquidation closer. Leverage does not raise expectancy, it raises risk.

stock.title: Stock position size (Nasdaq, NYSE)
stock.desc: How many whole shares to buy or short so the loss at your stop stays within the risk you chose. Includes per-share commission.
stock.note: Shares trade in whole units, so the result is rounded down. If the share of balance is above 100%, you need broker leverage or a smaller size. Not investment advice.

futures.title: Futures and gold risk (NQ, ES, GC, CL, XAUUSD)
futures.desc: How many contracts or lots fit your risk when the stop hits. Gold, silver, oil and indices: the point value is filled in from the contract.

c.14: XAUUSD — gold at a broker, 1 lot = 100 oz, $100 per $1

futures.note: Form size = contracts × point value, so profit and loss in Tartib come out right in dollars. Point values are for reference: check the exchange contract specs. Not investment advice.

fear.dominance: Bitcoin's share of the market cap: {v}%
fear.hint: Shows crypto market sentiment on a scale from 0 to 100. This is a reference indicator, not a signal.

movers.title: 24-hour leaders
movers.hint: USDT pairs with a daily turnover above 2 million (OKX, spot). Tap a pair to open its chart.

watch.title: Watchlist
watch.empty: Empty for now. Add the pairs you follow.

alerts.title: Price alerts
alerts.subtitle: When the price reaches the level you get a notification on the site and in Telegram. Checked every minute.

calendar.title: Events calendar
calendar.subtitle: Upcoming events this week, time zone: {tz}. Important news moves the market.

journal.title: Trade journal
journal.tagsHint: Comma-separated, up to 10. E.g. breakout, news
journal.gradeHint: A — followed the plan, D — many deviations. Grade how you stuck to the plan, not the profit.
journal.mistakesHint: Mark what went off plan. This is data for review, not a judgement of you.
journal.closedAtHint: If empty, duration is not calculated
journal.closeText: Enter the exit price — the result is calculated for you.
journal.closeTimeHint: If empty, the current time is used
journal.errClosedBefore: Close time cannot be before the open time
journal.fromClone: This is a copy of a trade: check prices and time before saving.
journal.templateText: Saves instrument, direction, strategy, tags and plan — without prices and time.
journal.templateSaved: Template saved. It will appear when you create a new trade.
journal.limitTemplates: You can keep at most 20 templates

an.mistakesHint: Result of trades where you marked this mistake. One trade can appear in several rows.
an.noMistakes: No trades with marked mistakes yet. Mark them in the trade form.
an.gradesHint: Shows whether trades made by the plan actually pay off.
an.noDuration: Needs a close time, which is set when you close a trade.

journal.mistakeNoteHint: In your own words: what you felt, what went wrong, what you will do differently. Only you can see this.

risk.title: System quality and risk
risk.subtitle: Figures are calculated from trades in the selected period. This is arithmetic on past trades, not a forecast.
risk.sqnHint: Shows how steady your results are in R. Higher means smoother profit per unit of risk.
risk.recoveryHint: Net profit divided by the maximum drawdown in money.
risk.waterHint: How many days the balance could not get back to its previous high.
risk.mathText: With {win}% winning trades and an average win to average loss of {payoff}, Kelly maths gives {kelly}% of the account per trade. At 1% risk per trade, the chance of ever losing 50% of the account in this model is {ruin}%.
risk.mathNote: The model assumes independent trades and constant numbers; it is a reference, not advice or a forecast.
risk.mathNone: Needs at least 20 trades, including both winners and losers.
risk.weekdayHint: Time zone comes from your settings.
risk.weekdayNone: No trades in this period yet.

diary.title: Day diary
diary.subtitle: Plan and mood in the morning, result and lesson in the evening. After a couple of weeks you can see how your state affects results.
diary.scaleHint: From 1 (bad) to 5 (great). Tap again to clear.
diary.planHint: What you trade, where you enter, when you stop. Keep it short.
diary.reviewHint: What worked, what did not, and why.
diary.lessonHint: One sentence you want to remember.
diary.readOnly: Entries older than 14 days are read-only.
diary.errDay: You cannot write for this day: today and the last 14 days only.
diary.streak: Days in a row with an entry
diary.planEffectNone: Mark in your day review whether you followed the plan and a comparison will appear here.
diary.moodNone: Needs entries with mood at two or more different ratings and days with trades.
diary.moodNote: Average over days with trades. This is an observation, not cause and effect. Days counted:

report.title: Printable report
report.hint: The print dialog will open. Choose “Save as PDF” to get a file.

start.title: First steps
start.subtitle: {done} of {total} done. Do only what is useful to you.

steps.journal: Add tags, a grade or mistakes to a trade
steps.diary: Write your first day diary entry

hero.hintNone: No trades today. Plan first: write it in your diary, then open a position.
hero.hintViolated: There is a trade with a rule violation today. Stop and reread your rules before opening the next one.
hero.hintLosing: The day is in the red. That is normal. Check your daily limit and your rules, not the urge to win it back.
hero.hintOk: Every trade today followed your rules. Keep this pace; the result is secondary.
hero.hintLimit: Your daily loss limit is reached. Your own rule says: enough for today. Close the terminal and come back tomorrow.
hero.hintPause: Several losses in a row. Take a 15–30 minute break, stand up, walk, then reread your plan.
hero.pauseBanner: {n} losses in a row, the last one {m} min ago. Take a 15–30 minute break and reread your plan before opening a new trade.

week.title: Week review
week.subtitle: The last 7 days against the previous 7. One takeaway and a few numbers.
week.empty: No trades in the last 7 days. Record one and the review will appear here.
week.takeRule: Biggest leak this week: the rule “{name}” was broken in {n} trades, net {amount}. Think about what stops you following it and write it in your diary.
week.takeMistake: Most expensive mistake this week: “{name}”, {n} trades, net {amount}. Tag it in your trades to catch the moment earlier.
week.takeDiscipline: Discipline {pct}% against a {goal}% goal. The result is secondary: first bring back the share of trades made by your rules.
week.takeSteady: No serious leaks this week: rules were mostly followed. Keep up the journal and the diary.
week.note: The takeaway is built from your records by simple rules; it is not a forecast.

usmarket.title: US market
usmarket.tz: Times in your zone ({tz}), trading day: {day}.
usmarket.note: NYSE and Nasdaq hours: pre-market 4:00–9:30, regular session 9:30–16:00, after-hours 16:00–20:00 New York time. Daylight saving is handled. Holiday dates are for reference; check the exchange calendar. Futures trade almost around the clock with their own hours.

usstats.title: Results by US market hours
usstats.hint: Stock and futures trades only. Times are New York time (daylight saving handled). Shows which hours you trade better and worse.
usstats.none: Needs stock or futures trades: pick the market in the trade form.

pdt.title: Day trades (PDT)
pdt.window: Stock trades opened and closed on the same day over the last {n} trading days (New York time).
pdt.ok: Day trades left before the limit: {n}.
pdt.warn: This is the maximum: the next day trade would be the fourth within 5 days.
pdt.flag: More than three day trades in 5 days. Check your account terms with the broker.
pdt.rule: For a margin account under ${limit}, 4 or more day trades in 5 trading days make you a pattern day trader.
pdt.notApplies: Your USD account equity is at least ${limit}, so this rule normally does not limit you.
pdt.note: The counter is for reference and only counts trades in your journal: confirm the rule with your broker.

mistakes.title: My mistakes
mistakes.subtitle: Trades with mistakes and broken rules are collected here. Mark what the mistake was, write why it happened and attach a screenshot.
mistakes.pasteHint: Paste a screenshot from the clipboard (Ctrl+V), drop it here or choose a file. Trades with broken rules appear here by themselves.
mistakes.worst: The costliest mistake is “{name}”: {n} trades, result {amount}.
mistakes.empty: Nothing yet. Once you mark a mistake in a trade or break a rule, the trade shows up here.
mistakes.todoHint: Check whether there was a mistake: if so, mark it and write the reason.

pm.title: Gains and losses
pm.subtitle: How much you made in winning trades, how much you lost in losing ones and where you end up.
pm.link: Gains and losses: income and spending
pm.accountNote: Deposits and withdrawals are recorded in Settings, in the accounts section. They are not part of the trading result.
pm.note: Trade results are after fees. This is record keeping, not a forecast.

worldmarkets.title: World markets
worldmarkets.subtitle: Gold and metals, oil and gas, currencies, indices, bonds and crypto. Tap a name to open its chart.
worldmarkets.note: Change versus the previous close. The source is unofficial (Yahoo Finance): data may be delayed and differ from your broker. Gold and silver are shown as COMEX futures, not the XAU/USD spot price. Rises in VIX, yields and the dollar have no colour: they are neither good nor bad. Not investment advice.

live.every5: Prices refresh by themselves every 5 seconds
live.paused: Updates paused: no connection to the source

tradertypes.title: Types of traders
tradertypes.subtitle: 30 types in 6 groups: by trade length, market, way of analysis, strategy, status and behaviour. One person usually combines several, for example “a day trader on Nasdaq, technical, trend-following”.
tradertypes.note: This is a reference classification: different sources split traders differently. The descriptions are not advice to trade in any particular way.
tradertypes.cta: Find your profile from your journal

you.title: Your trader profile
you.subtitle: Worked out from your journal. A hint based on your own records, not a diagnosis or advice.
you.need: At least 5 trades are needed to work out a profile. For style, trades must have a closing time.
you.needStyle: Style needs a closing time on 5 trades.

horizon.title: By how long trades are held
horizon.desc: The main split: how long a trader keeps a position.

market.title: By market
market.desc: Which market the trader works in.

analysis.title: By way of analysis
analysis.desc: What a trade decision rests on.

status.title: By status
status.desc: Whose money the trader uses and in what role.

behavior.title: By behaviour (what shows in the journal)
behavior.desc: Not a diagnosis but habits in trades. This is what Tartib helps you see.

scalper.name: Scalper
scalper.text: Holds a trade from seconds to a few minutes and makes many trades a day. Each gain is small, so fees and discipline matter most.

day.name: Day trader (intraday)
day.text: Opens and closes trades within one day and keeps no positions overnight. For US stocks the PDT rule applies.

swing.name: Swing trader
swing.text: Holds a trade from several days to several weeks and aims at larger price moves. No need to watch the screen all day.

position.name: Position trader
position.text: Holds a position for months and years, following long trends. Few trades, but swings along the way can be large.

hft.name: High-frequency (HFT)
hft.text: Robots of large firms make thousands of trades per second. Not available to ordinary private traders, yet they move part of the market.

crypto.name: Crypto trader
crypto.text: Trades cryptocurrencies. The market is open around the clock with no days off, and prices can move sharply.

forex.name: Forex trader
forex.text: Trades currency pairs such as EUR/USD. Many sessions a day, often with leverage.

stocks.name: Stock trader
stocks.text: Trades company shares on Nasdaq, NYSE and other exchanges. The market keeps exchange hours with pre-market and after-hours.

futures.name: Futures trader
futures.text: Trades contracts on indices, gold, oil and other assets. The point value is set by the contract and risk is counted in contracts.

commodities.name: Commodities and gold trader
commodities.text: Trades gold, silver, oil, gas and grain. Prices depend on politics, inventories and demand.

options.name: Options trader
options.text: Trades rights to buy or sell an asset at a set price. Risk and result depend on time and volatility, so separate study is needed.

technical.name: Technical trader
technical.text: Decides from the chart: levels, trends, indicators and candle patterns.

fundamental.name: Fundamental trader
fundamental.text: Looks at the economy, company reports, rates and the balance of supply and demand.

news.name: News trader
news.text: Trades around important data and events: inflation, rates, earnings. Moves are fast and slippage is large.

algo.name: Algorithmic trader
algo.text: Writes the rules as code and a robot enters and exits on its own. The main risks are code bugs and overfitting to the past.

discretionary.name: Discretionary trader
discretionary.text: Decides on the spot from experience without a rigid system. Depends most on discipline and emotions.

trend.name: Trend follower
trend.text: Trades with the direction of the move: buys in rises, sells in falls. Tolerates pullbacks while the trend lives.

countertrend.name: Counter-trend trader
countertrend.text: Looks for reversals and a return to the mean. Enters against the move, so the stop matters even more.

breakout.name: Breakout trader
breakout.text: Enters when price leaves a range or breaks a level. Some breakouts turn out false.

arbitrage.name: Arbitrage trader
arbitrage.text: Earns from price gaps for one asset across markets or between related instruments. Needs speed and low fees.

orderflow.name: Order-flow trader
orderflow.text: Reads the order book, the tape and volumes to see who pushes the price. Usually scalpers and day traders.

retail.name: Private (retail) trader
retail.text: Trades their own money through a broker. Tartib is made for this trader.

prop.name: Prop trader
prop.text: Trades the firm's money and shares the profit with it. Strict drawdown limits usually apply, and breaking them ends access.

institutional.name: Institutional trader
institutional.text: Works at a bank, fund or investment firm with large sums. Decisions follow procedures under risk management.

manager.name: Money manager (copy trading, PAMM)
manager.text: Trades other people's money and answers to them for results. Transparent records and drawdown control matter most.

systematic.name: Systematic
systematic.text: Enters and exits by their own rules and follows the plan in most trades. Results can be judged by numbers rather than mood.

impulsive.name: Impulsive
impulsive.text: Often enters from fear of missing out or greed and chases price. A pre-trade checklist and a pause help.

revenge.name: Revenge trader
revenge.text: After a loss wants the money back at once and enters without a plan. A daily loss limit and a pause after a losing run help.

overtrader.name: Overtrader
overtrader.text: Makes too many trades, often without strong signals, and pays fees. A limit on trades per day helps.

cautious.name: Cautious
cautious.text: More often closes a trade earlier than planned or enters with doubt and fear. It helps to check what early exits cost.
